rationale: Split: plain random 25% hold-out with the run seed, as specified (no stratification since the target is defined after the split). Target: paid_amount > 95th percentile with threshold_source=train_only, overriding the all_data default so the test partition cannot inform the threshold; the component records threshold_value and positive rate/count per partition into threshold.json. Features: only fields known at claim submission (claim type, CPT category, place of service, specialty, network status, units, length of stay, ER/elective/preventive/auth flags, primary diagnosis, DRG presence). Excluded all amount fields (billed, allowed, paid, member_oop, cob) because the target is derived from paid_amount and the others are adjudication outputs, plus high_cost_flag (a pre-computed label) and claim_id/member_id (identifiers); the catalogue default feature set was rejected because it contains billed_amount and allowed_amount. Preprocessing: fit_on=train_only to prevent encoder/scaler leakage; standard scaling aids logistic regression convergence across service_units and length_of_stay and is harmless for trees. Models: logistic regression plus gradient boosting as the single tree-based model, yielding PR-AUC, ROC-AUC and precision/recall at the top 5% of held-out claims. Report: denominators printed for every rate, every result cited to an artifact, and caveats for synthetic data, ~5% class prevalence, baseline-model limitations and no operational use.
